title_en: Tangshan Ceramics Association v. Li, et al. — dispute over unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: Regarding the issue of whether an industry association has standing as a plaintiff in an unfair competition dispute, a comprehensive determination may be made based on factors such as the nature and business scope of the industry association. If the industry association has a competitive relationship with the operator and has a direct interest in the case, it may be found to have proper plaintiff standing.

Li Mou, et al. - unfair competition dispute
full_text_en:
Tangshan Ceramic Association v. Li Mou, et al. — dispute over unfair competition

[Gist of the Judgment]

Whether a trade association has the standing as a plaintiff in an unfair competition dispute can be determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the nature of the trade association and its scope of business. If the trade association has a competitive relationship with the business operator and has a direct interest in the case, it can be determined to have proper plaintiff standing.

For a specific product name that has a national standard or industry standard, where there is no relevant evidence to confirm the existence of a succession relationship, prefixing the specific product name with "New (Xin)" as the advertised product name is likely to cause consumers to develop a mistaken understanding of the product, and has the potential to deceive or mislead consumers. Such an advertising practice can be considered as constituting false publicity.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Civil Re-Trial No. 76

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Tangshan Ceramic Association. Address: Tangshan City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Xia Moushi, President of the Association.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiaoyue, lawyer from Hebei Yuebin Law Firm.

Respondent (Shareholder of Changsha Shunmou E-commerce Co., Ltd., Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Li Mou, male, residing in Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Agent ad litem: Qi Wei, lawyer from Guangdong Jinqiao Baixin (Changsha) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Nengjia, trainee lawyer from Guangdong Jinqiao Baixin (Changsha) Law Firm.

Respondent (Shareholder of Changsha Shunmou E-commerce Co., Ltd., Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Zhang Mou, male, residing in Liling City, Hunan Province.

Agent ad litem: Qi Wei, lawyer from Guangdong Jinqiao Baixin (Changsha) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Nengjia, trainee lawyer from Guangdong Jinqiao Baixin (Changsha) Law Firm.

The re-applicant, Tangshan Ceramic Association, disagreed with the civil judgment (2020) Ji Min Zhong No. 104 of the Hebei High People's Court regarding its dispute with the respondent, Changsha Shunmou E-commerce Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changsha Shunmou Company), over unfair competition, and applied to this Court for a retrial. On December 11, 2021, this Court issued the civil ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 114, granting a retrial of this case. During the retrial proceedings, Changsha Shunmou Company was dissolved. This Court notified its shareholders, Li Mou and Zhang Mou, to participate in the proceedings. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing in this case. The agent ad litem of the re-applicant, Tangshan Ceramic Association, Li Xiaoyue, and the common agent ad litem of the respondents, Li Mou and Zhang Mou, Qi Wei, appeared before the court. The hearing has now concluded.

Tangshan Ceramic Association applied for a retrial, stating: The original judgment was erroneous in both fact-finding and application of law. It requested this Court to revoke the first and second instance judgments and order the Hebei High People's Court to conduct a retrial. The main facts and reasons are as follows: (i) Bone china is a high-grade porcelain originating from England with a history of over three hundred years. Through 17 years of continuous exploration by the older generation of ceramic craftsmen in Tangshan, China's first batch of bone china was successfully developed in 1974, ending China's history of not producing bone china. The social reputation of Chinese bone china was mainly created and earned by Tangshan bone china enterprises. The national standard for bone china has clear provisions for the content of tricalcium phosphate. Changsha Shunmou Company promoted products that are not bone china as "New Bone China (Xin Gu Ci)," passing off inferior products as quality ones. This constitutes the unfair competition act of false publicity. It not only damages the good reputation of bone china but also infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of the Tangshan Ceramic Association and its members. The second instance judgment's finding that Changsha Shunmou Company's false publicity would not adversely affect the Tangshan Ceramic Association lacked factual basis. (ii) Although the Tangshan Ceramic Association is a non-profit entity, as an industry organization for Tangshan bone china producers and the owner of the collective trademark "Tangshan Bone China," it is a service provider for the brand and quality of the bone china market. It has the responsibility to protect its own and its members' legitimate rights and interests, as well as the reputation of bone china. (iii) The Tangshan Ceramic Association has the right to choose legal avenues such as civil litigation or administrative remedies. The second instance judgment's conclusion that the Tangshan Ceramic Association did not have the right to demand Changsha Shunmou Company to cease its advertising and compensate for losses through civil litigation, and could only report the matter to the relevant regulatory authorities, lacked legal basis. (iv) The second instance judgment applied the law inconsistently. If it believed the Tangshan Ceramic Association had standing, it should have supported its substantive claims. If it believed there was no standing, it should have dismissed the association's lawsuit. Since the second instance court deemed the Tangshan Ceramic Association had no direct interest in the case, it should not have made a substantive ruling. (v) Before filing this lawsuit, the Tangshan Ceramic Association commissioned a lawyer to file a complaint with the Hangzhou Market Supervision Administration. However, the administrative authority replied that "New Bone China" did not constitute false publicity. Out of necessity, the association filed this civil lawsuit to regulate the unfair competitive behavior of Changsha Shunmou Company and others. (vi) According to the evidence submitted by the Tangshan Ceramic Association at first instance, the sales volume and cumulative evaluations of Changsha Shunmou Company's New Bone China tableware were relatively high. Currently, over a dozen enterprises use "New Bone China" for false publicity, causing serious adverse effects on the bone china industry. If the court believes that only individual enterprises can serve as plaintiffs, requiring hundreds of bone china producers and sellers to sue Changsha Shunmou Company separately would undoubtedly cause heavy litigation burdens on the defendants. Additionally, the court would face difficulties in calculating damages. Having the industry association sue to stop Changsha Shunmou Company's false publicity can conserve judicial resources.

Li Mou and Zhang Mou stated in their defense: (i) Changsha Shunmou Company's use of the term "New Bone China" does not constitute false publicity. The second instance judgment's finding that Changsha Shunmou Company committed false publicity was erroneous in both fact-finding and application of law. 1. According to the purchasing habits of consumers on online shopping platforms and general porcelain consumers, they judge products based on the ingredients indicated by the merchants. Changsha Shunmou Company never claimed that the products sold contained "bone ash" or had any connection with "Tangshan Bone China." Instead, it explicitly stated that the products sold were "porcelain." This is insufficient to mislead the general public. 2. The Tangshan Ceramic Association provided no evidence that Changsha Shunmou Company's advertising could potentially mislead the public or directly harm the association. 3. The Tangshan Ceramic Association filed a complaint with the Hangzhou Market Supervision Administration, which responded that the merchant's use of the term "New Bone China" did not constitute false publicity. (ii) The Tangshan Ceramic Association is a non-profit legal entity and does not have a commercial competitive relationship with Changsha Shunmou Company. (iii) Even if Changsha Shunmou Company's actions were considered false publicity, the products it sells would not create a specific association with the Tangshan Ceramic Association or its identifiers, nor would they harm the association's rights. 1. New Bone China is essentially a type of white porcelain. By adding different proportions of raw materials like feldspar, quartz, and kaolin, it affects the firing temperature, deformation, water absorption, and translucency of traditional porcelain, creating a new material. New Bone China products possess the excellent properties of bone china while having the advantages of simpler production processes and lower production costs. Due to the expanding market share of New Bone China, the Tmall platform has added "New Bone China" to its current product categories, and many merchants on the platform use the term "New Bone China" to sell products. 2. Articles such as "The Difference Between Bone China and New Bone China" published in the industry journal "Ceramics" not only acknowledge the status of New Bone China but also recognize the commercial value it brings. 3. The reputation of New Bone China stems from its own performance characteristics, not from riding on the coattails of "Bone China." Changsha Shunmou Company did not mention anything related to "Tangshan" or "Tangshan Bone China" in its advertising or product sales, nor did it engage in any other conduct likely to cause consumers to mistakenly associate "New Bone China" with the Tangshan Ceramic Association. (iv) The Tangshan Ceramic Association is not asserting trademark or geographical indication protection. Its claims should not expand the scope of protection and restrict normal market competition. Terms like "Bone China," "Bone Porcelain," and "New Bone China" are descriptive words for porcelain products and should not be used as identifiers to distinguish providers of goods or services. (v) The procedures of the original trial court were proper. Since Changsha Shunmou Company did not engage in unfair competition, the Tangshan Ceramic Association's claims lacked factual and legal basis and should not be upheld. In conclusion, they requested upholding the original judgment and dismissing the Tangshan Ceramic Association's retrial application.

The Tangshan Ceramic Association filed a lawsuit with the Tangshan Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province (hereinafter referred to as the first instance court), requesting: 1. A judgment ordering Changsha Shunmou Company to immediately cease the unfair competition act of false publicity and refrain from using the term "Bone China" on non-bone china products it sells. 2. A judgment ordering Changsha Shunmou Company to compensate the Tangshan Ceramic Association for losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 100,000. 3. A judgment ordering Changsha Shunmou Company to publish a statement in the media within its sales region, clarifying that the "New Bone China" tableware it produces and sells are ceramic products, not bone china products. 4. The litigation costs of this case to be borne by Changsha Shunmou Company.

Changsha Shunmou Company argued: 1. The Tangshan Ceramic Association is not a proper party to this case and does not have standing. 2. "New Bone China" and "Bone China" are different types of porcelain; "New Bone China" does not constitute false publicity. It requested the dismissal of the Tangshan Ceramic Association's claims.

The Tangshan Ceramic Association submitted the following evidence to the first instance court:

First Set of Evidence:
1. Trademark Registration Certificate for "Tangshan Bone China," showing the Tangshan Ceramic Association is the registrant of this geographical indication collective trademark.
2. Charter of the Tangshan Ceramic Association, Article 2 of which states the association's purposes include: protecting the legitimate rights and interests of this industry, supervising self-discipline among enterprises, serving the industry, serving members, and promoting the prosperous development of the Tangshan ceramics industry. Evidence 1 and 2 aim to prove that the Tangshan Ceramic Association is a proper plaintiff in this case with standing.
3. Civil Judgment (2005) Hai Min Chu Zi No. 16146 of the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing and Civil Judgment (2006) Yi Zhong Min Zhong Zi No. 5251 of the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, aiming to prove that there are precedents for trade associations being parties in unfair competition dispute litigation.

Second Set of Evidence:
1. Certificates of Honor issued by Shanghai Jin Jiang International Hotel (Group) Co., Ltd. and the Expo Center Jin Jiang VIP Guest Service Management Department, showing that during the 2010 Shanghai World Expo, the sales branch of Tangshan Taomou Co., Ltd. provided quality products to the Expo Center Jin Jiang VIP Guest Service Management Department. A certificate of award from September 2016 issued by the Hangzhou International Expo Center, showing "Outstanding Contribution Award for G20 Hangzhou Summit Service Guarantee."
2. Certificates for the authorized use of the Tangshan Bone China geographical indication by Tangshan Demou Co., Ltd. and Tangshan Longmou Co., Ltd., and certificates of honor for these two enterprises. An appraisal showing that as of December 31, 2012, the "De Meilan" trademark of Tangshan Demou Co., Ltd. was valued at RMB 19.6 million. In June 2017, the bone china of Tangshan Longmou Co., Ltd. was rated "Hebei Province Quality Product" by the Hebei Provincial Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision. In January 2018, the Longchang brand household porcelain produced by Tangshan Longmou Co., Ltd. was awarded "China Ceramic Industry Famous Brand" by the China Ceramic Industry Association. In November 2017, the hand-painted fine bone china of Tangshan Yamou Ceramics Co., Ltd. was named "Beautiful Hebei Outstanding Brand Product" by the Propaganda Department of the Hebei Provincial Party Committee and the Hebei Provincial Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision.
3. A certificate issued in December 2018 by the China Ceramic Industry Association to Tangshan Longmou Co., Ltd. for "China Ceramic Industry Technological Innovation Advanced Enterprise." A "Hebei Province Industrial Enterprise R&D Institution Certificate" issued in December 2017 by the Hebei Provincial Department of Industry and Information Technology to the R&D Center of Longmou Bone China Co., Ltd., classified as self-built (A-level). The second set of evidence aims to prove that Tangshan bone china has a high reputation and brand value domestically, and that related enterprises continuously invest in R&D for bone china.

Third Set of Evidence:
1. Sales voucher dated April 9, 2019. Aiming to prove that the ceramic product used by the Tangshan Ceramic Association for testing tricalcium phosphate content was purchased from Changsha Shunmou Company's Tmall store, Yi Mou Flagship Store.
2. Two inspection reports from the National Light Industry Ceramic Quality Supervision and Testing Tangshan Station, National Inspection (Tao) Zi (2019) Nos. 275 and 276. These show that for ceramic products sold by Changsha Shunmou Company bearing the "New Bone China" label, the sample named "Green Chinese Style New Bone China Tableware Set" had a tricalcium phosphate content of 0.81%; the sample named "Spring Grass Chinese Style New Bone China Tableware Set" had a tricalcium phosphate content of 0.86%. Aiming to prove that the tricalcium phosphate content of the above samples was far below the 36% national standard for bone china, and they are not qualified bone china.
3. Trusted Timestamp Certification Certificate, for fixing webpage information regarding Changsha Shunmou Company's ceramic product sales on May 13, 2019. The webpage information shows: the product material is described as "porcelain," the product name is "Bowl and Plate Set Yijia Chinese Style New Bone China Tableware Set Simple Ceramic Bowls and Plates Home Use Gift Giving Green," the price is RMB 394.9 per set, and the monthly sales volume is shown as 190 units. Aiming to prove that Changsha Shunmou Company engaged in false publicity.
4. Trusted Timestamp Certification Certificate, for fixing the related recording of the Yi Mou Flagship Store on May 13, 2019. Aiming to prove the continuity of the webpage evidence collection and that it was not subsequently altered.
5. Sales voucher from the purchase on May 24, 2019, and Trusted Timestamp Certification Certificate for the video recording of the courier packaging and receipt. Aiming to prove that the second purchase of ceramic products was kept intact for the court's verification.
6. Trusted Timestamp Certification Certificate, for fixing the webpage where the "material" field in the product details section could be modified. Aiming to prove that the "material" information in the product details section can be modified.

Fourth Set of Evidence:
1. Query results from the Gongbiao website regarding the ICS international standard professional classification directory for ceramics. Aiming to prove that China has established product standards for all types of porcelain, including bone china and antibacterial bone china. "New Bone China" has no standard in China and is not a new type of porcelain.
2. A notarized document (2018) Ji Tang Hua Zheng Jing Zi No. 58 from Huayi Notary Office of Tangshan City, Hebei Province. Aiming to prove that some enterprises name their products "Moonlight Bone China."
3. Timestamp fixing of the webpage for "Jialan New Bone China Bowl Ceramic Bowl Home 6 Piece Set Elegant 5-inch Tall Bowl Rice Bowl Noodle Bowl Gift Bowl Set," product inspection report, and physical sample.
4. Timestamp fixing of the webpage for "Duoyi Vintage Tableware Pointed Bottom Bowl New Bone China Rice Bowl Fruit Salad Bowl Creative Soup Bowl Noodle Bowl Home Large Bowl," product inspection report, and physical sample. Evidence 3 and 4 aim to prove that ceramic products of different quality levels also claim to be "New Bone China."

Fifth Set of Evidence:
1. One invoice for the purchase of ceramic products on April 10, 2019, showing expenditure of RMB 729.8.
2. Purchase voucher dated May 24, 2019, showing expenditure of RMB 789.8. The fifth set of evidence aims to prove part of the Tangshan Ceramic Association's rights protection expenditures.

Changsha Shunmou Company presented the following objections to the evidence:

Regarding the first set of evidence: Evidence 3 is a judgment made before the revision of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and is not applicable to this case.

Regarding the second set of evidence: Relevance is not acknowledged, as the bone china brand value mentioned by the Tangshan Ceramic Association is irrelevant to this case.

Regarding the third set of evidence: The authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 1 are acknowledged. The relevance of Evidence 2 is not acknowledged; this evidence exactly proves that New Bone China is not bone china. The authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 3 are acknowledged, but the purpose of proof is not accepted; this evidence cannot prove that our company engaged in false publicity for the products. The authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 4 and 5 are acknowledged. The purpose of proof of Evidence 6 is not accepted. Although the material information in the product details section can be modified, upon investigation, the material field for items listed on the Tmall platform in 2013 did not include New Bone China.

Regarding the fourth set of evidence: The relevance and purpose of proof are not admitted. This set of evidence does not mention New Bone China.

Regarding the fifth set of evidence: Authenticity, legality, and relevance are all acknowledged.

Changsha Shunmou Company submitted the following evidence:

First Set of Evidence: Business registration information of the Tangshan Ceramic Association and webpage screenshots from the Tangshan Ceramic Association's official website. Aiming to prove that the Tangshan Ceramic Association is a non-profit legal entity and lacks standing.

Second Set of Evidence: Online store cooperation agreement between Changsha Shunmou Company and Hunan Huamou Household Products Co., Ltd., Huanou supplier cooperation agreement, procurement contracts for the products in question, an inspection report from the National Light Industry Ceramic Quality Supervision and Testing Liling Station, etc. Aiming to prove that the online store run by Changsha Shunmou Company for selling the products in question is a legally authorized Tmall flagship store, and all products sold are produced by regular manufacturers with quality assurance. The products in question are of qualified quality and the material is "New Bone China"; there is no false publicity.

Third Set of Evidence: 1. Webpage screenshots of other merchants selling this type of product on the Tmall platform. Aiming to prove that it is common practice for Tmall merchants selling "New Bone China" products to select "Porcelain" under the material field. 2. Articles from the industry journal "Ceramics" titled "The Difference Between Bone China and New Bone China," from the journal "China Ceramics" titled "Preliminary Exploration of New Bone China," and from the journal "Hebei Ceramics" titled "Development of Low-Temperature Single-Firing New Bone China Using Porcelain Clay." These articles aim to prove that "New Bone China" is not "Bone China."

The Tangshan Ceramic Association presented the following objections to the evidence:

Regarding the first set of evidence: Authenticity, legality, and relevance are acknowledged; the purpose of proof is not accepted. The webpage screenshot indicates that the purposes of the Tangshan Ceramic Association include protecting the legitimate rights and interests of this industry.

Regarding the second set of evidence: Relevance is not acknowledged. The inspection report from the National Light Industry Ceramic Quality Supervision and Testing Liling Station is a test of ordinary ceramics and has no relation to bone china.

Regarding the third set of evidence: Authenticity is acknowledged; the purpose of proof is not accepted. The articles in the journals represent personal views and have not been recognized by the industry or the state. Moreover, the products of Changsha Shunmou Company in this case were not made according to the formula in the article "The Difference Between Bone China and New Bone China." The article states that although both bone china and new bone china contain "tricalcium phosphate," the tricalcium phosphate in bone china comes from natural bone ash in animal remains, while the tricalcium phosphate in new bone china is artificially synthesized. Bone china contains over 40% bone ash, while new bone china contains no bone ash.

The facts found by the trial court:

Tangshan Ceramics Association is the registrant of the geographical indication collective trademark "Tangshan Bone China," with registration number No. 16325979. The approved goods/services fall under Class 21: household ceramic products; daily-use porcelain; porcelain decorations; porcelain, ceramic, earthenware, or glass figurines, etc. The registration date is January 14, 2016, and the validity period extends to January 13, 2026. Tangshan Ceramics Association is a local, industry-specific social organization voluntarily formed by ceramic enterprises, related entities, and individual members in Tangshan City, and is a non-profit social organization. Its business scope includes: establishing industry self-regulatory mechanisms, formulating industry regulations and conventions, maintaining industry competition order, organizing professional training and exchanges, and providing consulting services. On April 9, 2019, Tangshan Ceramics Association purchased ceramic products sold by Changsha Shun Company from a Tmall platform store named "Yi Mou Flagship Store (i* Flagship Store)." The product name was "Green Dinnerware Set Yi Jia Chinese New Bone China Tableware Set Simple Ceramic Bowls Chopsticks Plates Home Use Gift," and the payment amount was RMB 729.8. Tangshan Ceramics Association commissioned the Tangshan Station of National Light Industry Ceramic Quality Supervision and Inspection to test the Green Chinese New Bone China tableware set purchased from Changsha Shun Company. The test result showed a tricalcium phosphate content of 0.81%, which did not meet the standard for bone china. Changsha Shun Company is the sole authorized dealer of Hunan Hua Mou Homeware Products Co., Ltd. on the Tmall platform. The ceramic products involved in the case sold by Changsha Shun Company were obtained from legitimate channels.

The court of first instance held that Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law), as amended in 2019, stipulates: "Business operators shall, in their production and business operations, follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, and comply with laws and business ethics. For the purposes of this Law, 'acts of unfair competition' refer to acts by business operators in their production and business operations that violate the provisions of this Law, disrupt the order of market competition, and harm the legitimate rights and interests of other business operators or consumers. For the purposes of this Law, 'business operators' refer to natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations engaged in the production or sale of goods or the provision of services (hereinafter, goods include services)." Tangshan Ceramics Association, as an unincorporated organization and the owner of the collective trademark "Tangshan Bone China," can serve as the litigation subject in this case. Tangshan Ceramics Association claimed that the promotional and sales conduct of Changsha Shun Company disrupted the market economy and constituted unfair competition. The material of the products sold by Changsha Shun Company is new bone china, not "bone china." Moreover, bone china is a type of porcelain, not a product unique or exclusive to Tangshan. Tangshan Ceramics Association, as the owner of the "Tangshan Bone China" trademark, has no evidence proving that Changsha Shun Company, in promoting or selling its products, established a specific connection between the products involved and Tangshan, i.e., that the ceramic products sold were produced in Tangshan rather than other regions, or that they were bone china products produced by Tangshan-related enterprises. Therefore, the claim of Tangshan Ceramics Association was not supported. Tangshan Ceramics Association's claim that Changsha Shun Company passed off inferior products as high-quality ones and damaged the reputation of bone china products lacked sufficient grounds and was not supported. In summary, in accordance with Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the court of first instance rendered the judgment: dismissing all litigation claims of Tangshan Ceramics Association. The case acceptance fee of RMB 2,300 was to be borne by Tangshan Ceramics Association.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of the first instance, Tangshan Ceramics Association appealed to the Hebei High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance), requesting: to reverse the judgment of the first instance and amend the judgment to support the litigation claims of Tangshan Ceramics Association in the first instance; and to have Changsha Shun Company bear the case acceptance fees for both the first and second instances. The main facts and reasons were: (1) The finding of the court of first instance that "the material of the products sold by Changsha Shun Company is new bone china" lacked factual and legal basis. Currently, the authority to name the categories of ceramics in China is jointly exercised by the State Administration for Market Regulation and the Standardization Administration of China; a people's court has no authority to determine the category name for a ceramic product. Bone china includes three categories: bone china, antibacterial bone china, and Zibo synthetic bone china. There is no such category or name as "new bone china." (2) There is no unified standard for "new bone china," and there are significant differences between new bone china products sold by different merchants. Merchants claiming that ceramics which are not bone china are new bone china essentially ride on the good reputation of bone china to increase their own sales share. This act violates the principle of good faith, misleads consumers, weakens the quality characteristics of bone china, and damages the market reputation of bone china. (3) The false propaganda of Changsha Shun Company directly harmed the interests of bone china production and sales enterprises in Tangshan. Tangshan Ceramics Association filed this lawsuit in accordance with the will of its member enterprises and in compliance with the association's charter. (4) If people's courts permit goods of different materials and attributes to be promoted by adding the word "new" before a generic name, this will encourage free-riding behavior and bring about serious adverse consequences to society.

In its defense, Changsha Shun Company argued that: (1) When purchasing bone china, ordinary consumers pay special attention to the product's characteristics and inevitably to the "bone powder" content, which is its main component. New bone china and bone china will not cause confusion among consumers. (2) Changsha Shun Company neither engaged in false propaganda, nor sought to exploit the goodwill of bone china, nor passed off inferior products as high-quality ones. (3) Tangshan Ceramics Association does not enjoy all legal rights related to "bone china" directly. Changsha Shun Company's promotion or sale of goods did not establish a specific connection with "Tangshan" or "Tangshan Bone China," and did not infringe upon any rights of Tangshan Ceramics Association. Therefore, Tangshan Ceramics Association's claims should not be supported.

During the second instance, Tangshan Ceramics Association submitted a set of evidence, including: 1. The "Tangshan City Annals" published by Local Records Press in November 1999, stating that a certain Tangshan ceramic factory produced daily-use export porcelain and was the only domestic manufacturer of high-quality bone china, successfully trial producing "Emerald" brand high-quality bone china in 1974. Mass production of bone china was expanded after the 1976 earthquake. In 1981, "Red Rose" brand high-quality white bone china was successfully developed and, upon appraisal by the State Science and Technology Commission and the Ministry of Light Industry, was confirmed to meet high-grade porcelain standards and was put into formal production. In 1984, the "Red Rose" brand tableware won the national silver medal. Except for a portion for export, most products were sold exclusively to over 80 high-end hotels and restaurants domestically. 2. Screenshots from Baidu Baike and 360 Encyclopedia regarding "bone china," stating that Tangshan is the birthplace of Chinese bone china, and currently over 80% of domestic sales and export bone china products come from Tangshan; bone china is recognized both domestically and internationally as high-grade porcelain. Evidence 1 and 2 were intended to prove the history, prestige, and market share of Tangshan bone china. 3. An invention patent certificate dated July 10, 1993, with patent number ZL89101452.7, patentee being the First Porcelain Factory of Tangshan Tao Mou Industrial Company, and title "Soft Bone China and its Manufacturing Method," which has since lapsed. This was intended to prove that Tangshan once held an invention patent for soft bone china and its manufacturing method, had continuously invested in the research and development of bone china, and that Tangshan ceramic enterprises made significant contributions to improving the quality of bone china. Changsha Shun Company acknowledged the authenticity of Evidence 1 and 2 but did not acknowledge the authenticity of Evidence 3 and did not acknowledge the purposes of proof.

The court of second instance found that during the first instance, both parties acknowledged that an important testing standard for bone china was a tricalcium phosphate content of no less than 36%. According to the test report for the ceramic products involved submitted by Tangshan Ceramics Association, the tricalcium phosphate content was 0.81%, far below the above standard. Additionally, Changsha Shun Company used the term "new bone china" in the name of the involved product. No other promotional statements related to Tangshan Ceramics Association appeared elsewhere on the webpage.

The court of second instance confirmed the other facts found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the focal points of the dispute were: First, whether Changsha Shun Company's conduct constituted false propaganda, and if so, whether such false propaganda constituted unfair competition against Tangshan Ceramics Association; Second, if it constituted unfair competition, how should Changsha Shun Company bear civil liability in this case.

Regarding whether it constitutes false propaganda: According to Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, which stipulates that "a business operator shall not make false or misleading commercial propaganda on its goods' performance, functions, quality, sales, user reviews, honors, etc., to deceive or mislead consumers," the above-mentioned promotional conduct of a business operator may constitute false propaganda. First, in this case, Changsha Shun Company used the words "Green Dinnerware Set Yi Jia Chinese New Bone China Tableware Set Simple Ceramic Bowls Chopsticks Plates Home Use Gift" as the name of the involved ceramic product for promotion on its Tmall store. The term "new bone china" was used as a keyword describing the quality or material of the product. Considering that relevant consumers on the involved Tmall platform often search for goods by using keywords, and "bone china" is clearly a keyword for searching for such bone china products, the alleged infringing conduct of Changsha Shun Company had the effect of guiding or attracting consumers. Second, according to the test report for the involved ceramic product provided by Tangshan Ceramics Association, the test result showed a tricalcium phosphate content of 0.81%, far from meeting the national standard requirement of at least 36% for bone china products. Therefore, the involved ceramic product was not a bone china product. Changsha Shun Company also acknowledged this fact, admitting that the "new bone china" product involved was essentially a type of white porcelain, not bone china. Third, bone china products, as a high-end series of ceramic products, derive their good quality from more complex and refined manufacturing processes and more expensive bone powder raw materials. Changsha Shun Company claimed that its product could, by merely adjusting the raw material ratio of existing ceramic products, approximate the appearance and texture of bone china, and thus called it "new bone china." However, Changsha Shun Company did not submit corresponding evidence to confirm that its product was similar in quality to bone china. Its claimed similarities in "appearance, texture" and other qualities, lacking objective standards, were highly dependent on personal feelings and could not be objectively evaluated. Furthermore, this claim did not conform to normal market rules and was inconsistent with the reality that bone china products, despite their high price, still occupy the high-end market. Therefore, Changsha Shun Company's claim was insufficiently supported, and its propaganda of the product as "new bone china" lacked reasonable grounds. Finally, according to the evidence submitted by Tangshan Ceramics Association in the first instance, the "new bone china" category was not included in the ceramic categories determined by relevant administrative departments in China. The materials submitted by Changsha Shun Company were merely individual theoretical articles about "new bone china" and could not prove that "new bone china" is an officially recognized ceramic category. Thus, its designation of the product as "new bone china" also lacked a legal basis. In summary, under these circumstances, Changsha Shun Company described the involved ceramic product, which does not belong to or have a special connection with bone china, as "new bone china" and added this term to the product name for use as a search keyword by consumers. It lacked legitimate and legal justifications and could easily cause consumers to misunderstand the quality and material of the product, mistakenly believing that the product had a special relationship (such as iteration or substitution) with bone china products (in reality, there are differences in quality, and significant differences in the indicative tricalcium phosphate content and manufacturing process; no special relationship exists other than both being ceramic products), thereby influencing consumer choices. This conduct constitutes false propaganda under Article 8 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The court of first instance erred in its determination of the above facts, and this should be corrected.

Regarding whether Changsha Shun Company's conduct constitutes unfair competition against Tangshan Ceramics Association: Article 8 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law imposes both administrative liability and civil liability. All false propaganda is subject to administrative punishment, but not all false propaganda constitutes unfair competition against a specific entity and thus is subject to civil action. According to Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, as amended in 2017, for Tangshan Ceramics Association to claim that Changsha Shun Company's conduct constituted unfair competition against it in this case, it must be shown not only that Changsha Shun Company engaged in false propaganda objectively, but also that Tangshan Ceramics Association is a citizen, legal person, or other organization with a direct interest in the false propaganda conduct. In this case, although Changsha Shun Company's use of the term "new bone china" for the product might cause consumer misunderstanding regarding the connection between the product and bone china products, its propaganda did not mention the term "Tangshan bone china" related to Tangshan Ceramics Association, nor did it engage in other acts likely to mislead consumers into believing there was a special connection with Tangshan Ceramics Association. Under these circumstances, even though Tangshan Ceramics Association argued that Tangshan is the birthplace and an important production base of bone china in China, it should not, for this reason alone, have the right to demand via civil litigation that Changsha Shun Company cease its propaganda and compensate for losses. Tangshan Ceramics Association may report the matter to relevant supervisory and inspection departments in accordance with Articles 16 and 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, or report it to the relevant online sales platform.

As described above, Changsha Shun Company's false propaganda conduct did not constitute unfair competition against Tangshan Ceramics Association. Therefore, the court of second instance did not discuss the issue of how to bear civil liability.

The court of second instance held that the grounds of appeal of Tangshan Ceramics Association were partially established. Although the judgment of the first instance erred in determining the fact of whether false propaganda was constituted, the final substantive result was not improper, and the court of second instance sustained it. The judgment of the second instance was: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 2,300 was to be borne by Tangshan Ceramics Association.

During the retrial stage before this Court, Tangshan Ceramics Association submitted two sets of new evidence. The first set of evidence: a Hebei Province general VAT invoice dated April 4, 2018, and a bank receipt issued by Hebei Yuebin Law Firm, for an amount of RMB 30,000, intended to prove the attorney's fees incurred for rights protection in this case. The second set of evidence: a trusted timestamp authentication certificate for "Yi Mou Flagship Store" on the Tmall platform dated June 27, 2023, and a screenshot of the store's business information change notice, intended to prove that the involved Tmall store is still in operation but no longer uses the term "bone china" for the goods sold. During cross-examination, Li Mou and Zhang Mou argued that: for the first set of evidence, since no corresponding agency agreement or transfer records were provided, relevance was not recognized. For the second set of evidence, authenticity, legality, and relevance were recognized.

Li Mou and Zhang Mou submitted two sets of new evidence. The first set of evidence: a Registration Notice dated April 2, 2022 (Registration No. [2022] 7558), a Tax Clearance Certificate dated March 9, 2022 (Chang Kai Tax Qi Qing [2022] No. 3369), a basic registration form for domestic enterprises, minutes of Changsha Shun Company's shareholders' meeting, and a letter of commitment from all investors, intended to prove the deregistration of Changsha Shun Company. The second set of evidence: a "Change Explanation" issued by Li Mou and Zhang Mou, intended to prove the change of operator of Yi Mou Flagship Store. Tangshan Ceramics Association recognized the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the above evidence.

This Court made the following determinations regarding the new evidence: Regarding the first set of evidence submitted by Tangshan Ceramics Association, as there was no supporting evidence such as an agency agreement besides the invoice and receipt, it could not achieve its purpose of proof. Other evidence submitted by both parties was admitted.

This Court found upon retrial that Tangshan Ceramics Association is a social group legal person; the authenticity of the patent certificate submitted by Tangshan Ceramics Association during the second instance was recognized. Other facts found in the first and second instance judgments were basically accurate and were confirmed by this Court. Additionally, it was found that:

The national standard GB/T 13522-2008 for bone china indicates that one of the technical requirements is "the content of tricalcium phosphate in the product's biscuit body shall not be less than 36%." According to the current national standards for ceramics, there is no standard or terminology for new bone china.

Changsha Shun Company was established on February 26, 2014, with a registered capital of RMB 100,000, and its enterprise type was a limited liability company (natural person investment or holding). The company had two shareholders, Li Mou and Zhang Mou, each holding 50% of the shares. Due to a shareholders' resolution to dissolve, Changsha Shun Company was deregistered on April 2, 2022. On March 9, 2022, a letter of commitment signed by all investors, Li Mou and Zhang Mou, stated: "Before applying for deregistration, this enterprise has completed the settlement of all creditor-debtor relationships. There are no unsettled liquidation expenses, employee wages, social insurance contributions, statutory compensation, unpaid taxes payable, or other unsettled matters. The liquidation work has been fully completed. All investors of this enterprise are responsible for the truthfulness of the above commitments. If there is any illegal or dishonest conduct, all investors shall bear the corresponding legal consequences and responsibilities." The "Yi Mou Flagship Store" on the Tmall platform is still in operation, but the operator is no longer Changsha Shun Company, and the goods sold no longer use the term "bone china."

This Court holds that the focal issues in the retrial stage of this case are: First, whether Tangshan Ceramics Association can initiate this civil lawsuit and has standing as a qualified plaintiff; Second, whether the use of "new bone china" in propaganda by Changsha Shun Company constitutes false propaganda and unfair competition; Third, if it constitutes false propaganda and unfair competition, how should legal liability be borne.

I. Issue One: Whether Tangshan Ceramics Association can initiate this civil lawsuit and has standing as a qualified plaintiff

(1) Regarding the issue of initiating a civil lawsuit

Upon investigation, the Tangshan Ceramics Association initiated a civil lawsuit on the grounds that Changsha ShunMou Company's false publicity constituted unfair competition. Article 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "This Law is enacted to promote the healthy development of the socialist market economy, encourage and protect fair competition, stop acts of unfair competition, and protect the lawful rights and interests of business operators and consumers." According to the provisions of this legislative purpose, the legal interests protected by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law are multiple. Correspondingly, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law stipulates three different types of legal liability, including administrative liability, civil liability, and criminal liability. Regarding administrative liability for false publicity, Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "If a business operator, in violation of the provisions of Article 8 of this Law, makes false or misleading commercial publicity about its goods, or assists other business operators in making false or misleading commercial publicity by organizing false transactions or other means, the supervisory inspection department shall order the cessation of the illegal act and impose a fine of not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than RMB 1,000,000 but not more than RMB 2,000,000 shall be imposed, and the business license may be revoked. If a business operator, in violation of the provisions of Article 8 of this Law, publishes false advertisements, it shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China." Article 16, paragraph 1, provides for a reporting system: "Any unit or individual has the right to report suspected acts of unfair competition to the supervisory inspection department, and the supervisory inspection department shall, upon receiving the report, handle it in a timely manner in accordance with the law." Regarding civil liability for false publicity, Article 17, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provide: "If a business operator, in violation of the provisions of this Law, causes damage to others, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. If the lawful rights and interests of a business operator are harmed by an act of unfair competition, it may file a lawsuit with the people's court." According to the above provisions, administrative liability and civil liability for false publicity are two parallel liabilities, not that administrative liability takes precedence. A party may choose either to report to the supervisory inspection department for administrative investigation and punishment, or to choose the civil remedy channel of civil litigation, provided that the civil litigation meets the statutory conditions.

(B) Whether the Tangshan Ceramics Association has standing as a qualified plaintiff

This issue can be examined from two aspects: First, whether there is a competitive relationship between the parties. Article 2, paragraph 3, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "For the purposes of this Law, 'business operator' refers to a natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization that engages in the production or operation of goods or the provision of services (hereinafter 'goods' includes services)." Article 17, paragraph 2, provides: "If the lawful rights and interests of a business operator are harmed by an act of unfair competition, it may file a lawsuit with the people's court." Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "For a market entity that has a relationship with a business operator in production and business activities such as possible competition for transaction opportunities or impairment of competitive advantages, the people's court may recognize it as an 'other business operator' as defined in Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law." Second, whether the party filing the lawsuit has a direct interest in the case. Article 122 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, as amended in 2021, provides: "A lawsuit must meet the following conditions: (1) The plaintiff is a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a direct interest in the case; ..."

Specifically in this case, the Tangshan Ceramics Association is a local and industry-specific social organization voluntarily formed by Tangshan ceramic enterprises, relevant units, and individual members, and is a non-profit legal person. The association's charter and the "Social Organization Legal Person Registration Certificate" clearly state that its business scope includes "maintaining the order of industry competition." At the same time, the Tangshan Ceramics Association is the registrant of the geographical indication collective trademark "Tangshan Bone China," and the registrant of a collective trademark has the duty to effectively manage and control the trademark. The Tangshan Ceramics Association, when promoting and marketing Tangshan bone china, is a business operator engaged in commodity activities. In the process of promoting and marketing Tangshan bone china, maintaining the competitive order of the bone china industry, and the reputation of Tangshan bone china, the Tangshan Ceramics Association has a competitive relationship with Changsha ShunMou Company. The alleged publicity conduct of Changsha ShunMou Company may cause damage to the lawful rights and interests of the Tangshan Ceramics Association. The Tangshan Ceramics Association has a direct interest in this case and has standing as a qualified plaintiff.

In summary, the judgment of the second instance, which held that the Tangshan Ceramics Association did not have the right to demand Changsha ShunMou Company to stop the publicity and compensate for losses through civil litigation, was erroneous in its determination, and this Court hereby corrects it.

II. Whether the use of "new bone china" for publicity by Changsha ShunMou Company constitutes false publicity constituting unfair competition

Article 2, paragraph 2, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "For the purposes of this Law, 'act of unfair competition' refers to an act of a business operator in its production and business activities that, in violation of the provisions of this Law, disrupts the order of market competition and damages the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers." Article 8, paragraph 1, provides: "A business operator shall not make false or misleading commercial publicity about the performance, function, quality, sales status, user reviews, or awards received of its goods, thereby deceiving or misleading consumers." Article 17 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a business operator engages in any of the following acts, deceiving or misleading the relevant public, the people's court may recognize it as 'misleading commercial publicity' as provided in Article 8, paragraph 1, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law: (1) making one-sided publicity or comparison of goods; (2) using scientifically unproven views, phenomena, etc., as established facts for commodity publicity; (3) using ambiguous language for commercial publicity; (4) other commercial publicity acts sufficient to cause misunderstanding. The people's court shall determine misleading commercial publicity based on factors such as daily life experience, the general attention of the relevant public, the facts of misunderstanding, and the actual situation of the object being publicized."

(A) Whether the "new bone china" publicity made by Changsha ShunMou Company has sufficient basis

First, according to the test report issued by the National Light Industry Ceramics Quality Supervision and Testing Tangshan Station, the tricalcium phosphate content of the ceramic goods sold by Changsha ShunMou Company was 0.81%, far below the national standard requiring a tricalcium phosphate content of not less than 36% for bone china (bone porcelain). Therefore, the ceramic goods do not belong to bone china (bone porcelain). Changsha ShunMou Company acknowledged this fact and argued that what it called "new bone china" is not bone china (bone porcelain).

Second, as of the present, the ceramic categories determined by China's national standards do not include the "new bone china" ceramic category, and there is no national standard or industry-recognized standard for "new bone china." Changsha ShunMou Company also admitted that there is no unified standard for "new bone china."

Third, although Changsha ShunMou Company submitted some articles about "new bone china" published in academic journals, on the one hand, the content of these articles shows that the descriptions of the new bone china body formula are not uniform; on the other hand, these articles are mainly research and exploratory in nature and have not formed a theoretical or practical conclusion. Changsha ShunMou Company claimed that the appearance, texture, etc., of "new bone china" are similar to bone china, but in the absence of standards, such descriptions are highly dependent on individual perception and cannot be objectively evaluated. Therefore, the description of the ceramic goods sold by Changsha ShunMou Company as "new bone china" lacks a factual basis or sufficient grounds.

(B) Whether the "new bone china" publicity has the possibility of deceiving or misleading consumers and causing damage to the Tangshan Ceramics Association

First, Changsha ShunMou Company, when selling ceramic goods on its YiMou flagship store, used the publicity "bowl and plate set Yijia Chinese-style new bone china tableware set, simple ceramic bowls, plates, and chopsticks, home use, gift-giving, Green," in which the words "new bone china" served as a descriptive keyword for the material or quality of the goods, objectively playing a role in prompting or attracting consumers.

Second, whether the "new bone china" publicity has the possibility of deceiving or misleading consumers should be comprehensively determined based on daily life experience, the general attention of the relevant public, and the specific circumstances of the case. Although Changsha ShunMou Company did not indicate the "bone powder" content of the ceramic goods it sold or claim that they contained "bone powder," for ordinary consumers, the name of the ceramic goods is more attention-grabbing product information. The words "new bone china" in the product name not only indicate a close connection with bone china (bone porcelain), but also the word "new" suggests an improvement or innovation over bone china (bone porcelain), substantially influencing consumers' choice of ceramic goods. The "new bone china" publicity is likely to cause the relevant public to misunderstand the material, quality, type, etc., of the ceramic goods and thus make wrong choices. The "new bone china" publicity is sufficient to produce a misleading effect.

Third, bone china is a high-grade ceramic variety, and its characteristics, which distinguish it from other porcelain, are mainly two: one is a tricalcium phosphate content of over 36%, and the other is that it is made through a secondary firing process. The quality of bone china is determined by its materials and complex manufacturing process. Changsha ShunMou Company knew that the "new bone china" it sold was fundamentally different from bone china in terms of body material content and production process, and it had no sufficient basis to promote it to ordinary consumers as "new bone china," yet it still used the words "new bone china" in the product name. This conduct is sufficient to affect consumers' choices when faced with similar goods, thereby enabling Changsha ShunMou Company to obtain additional transaction opportunities directly or indirectly, harming the legitimate interests of bone china operators and disrupting the order of market competition. Although Changsha ShunMou Company's publicity did not mention the specific region of "Tangshan" or a connection with "Tangshan bone china," and the Tangshan Ceramics Association did not file a lawsuit based on trademark infringement, the Tangshan region is the main production area for bone china in China, and "Tangshan bone china" is a geographical indication collective trademark. The "new bone china" publicity will reduce the reputation of Tangshan bone china and may even bring negative evaluations to Tangshan bone china, causing the competitive advantage of the Tangshan Ceramics Association as an industry operator in the ceramic industry to diminish or be lost. The conduct in question damaged the lawful rights and interests of the Tangshan Ceramics Association.

Based on the above analysis, the use of "new bone china" for publicity by Changsha ShunMou Company constitutes false publicity constituting unfair competition. The judgment of the second instance, which held that Changsha ShunMou Company's false publicity did not constitute unfair competition against the Tangshan Ceramics Association, was erroneous in its determination, and this Court hereby corrects it.

III. If it constitutes false publicity unfair competition, how should legal liability be borne

Changsha ShunMou Company's false publicity unfair competition conduct caused damage to the Tangshan Ceramics Association. According to Article 17, paragraph 1, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. This case is a retrial case. The judgment of the second instance was rendered on May 28, 2020. The Civil Code of the People's Republic of China came into effect on January 1, 2021. Article 5 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a case has been finally adjudicated before the implementation of the Civil Code, and a party applies for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the provisions of the Civil Code shall not apply." Regarding the civil liability in this case, Article 15 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The main methods of bearing tort liability include: (1) cessation of infringement; (2) removal of obstacles; (3) elimination of danger; (4) return of property; (5) restoration to original condition; (6) compensation for losses; (7) apology; (8) elimination of adverse effects and restoration of reputation. The methods of bearing tort liability listed above may be applied individually or in combination." Article 17, paragraphs 3 and 4, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provide: "The amount of compensation for a business operator damaged by an act of unfair competition shall be determined according to the actual losses suffered by the business operator due to the infringement; if the actual losses are difficult to calculate, it shall be determined according to the benefits obtained by the infringer due to the infringement. ... The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses paid by the business operator to stop the infringement. If the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement or the benefits obtained by the infringer due to the infringement are difficult to determine for an act in violation of Article 6 or Article 9 of this Law, the people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the infringement, make a judgment awarding the right holder compensation of not more than RMB 5,000,000." Article 23 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "For unfair competition acts specified in Articles 2, 8, 11, and 12 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, if the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement or the benefits obtained by the infringer due to the infringement are difficult to determine, and the party claims to determine the amount of compensation in accordance with Article 17, paragraph 4, of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the people's court shall support it."

Regarding cessation of infringement. In the first instance, the Tangshan Ceramics Association requested a judgment ordering Changsha ShunMou Company to immediately cease the false publicity unfair competition conduct and not to use the word "bone china" in the sale of its non-bone china ceramic goods. Changsha ShunMou Company's "new bone china" publicity constitutes false publicity unfair competition, and the company shall cease the unfair competition conduct in accordance with the law. However, based on the facts ascertained by this Court during the retrial, the online store previously operated by Changsha ShunMou Company is currently not using the words "new bone china" for publicity, and the alleged unfair competition conduct has ceased; the actual operator of the store has changed and is no longer Changsha ShunMou Company. Given the above circumstances, this Court does not support this claim.

Regarding elimination of adverse effects. In the first instance, the Tangshan Ceramics Association requested a judgment ordering Changsha ShunMou Company to declare in the media of its sales region that the "new bone china" tableware it produces and sells is not bone china products. Given that the online store in question has ceased using "new bone china" publicity, which can help eliminate consumer confusion, this Court does not support this claim.

Regarding compensation for losses. In the first instance, the Tangshan Ceramics Association requested a judgment ordering Changsha ShunMou Company to compensate for the losses sustained by the Tangshan Ceramics Association and the reasonable expenses for rights protection, totaling RMB 100,000. The Tangshan Ceramics Association provided invoices and documents for two purchases of ceramic goods, totaling RMB 1,519.60. Although the Tangshan Ceramics Association did not provide corresponding evidence for the lawyer's fees and testing fees claimed as rights protection expenses, these expenses actually occurred and may be considered together in the amount of compensation. The actual losses suffered by the Tangshan Ceramics Association due to the infringement and the benefits obtained by Changsha ShunMou Company due to the infringement are both difficult to calculate. This Court, comprehensively considering factors such as the nature, circumstances, and duration of Changsha ShunMou Company's infringement, determines that the compensation for economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights protection to the Tangshan Ceramics Association shall be RMB 50,000.

Regarding the subject bearing civil liability. During the retrial of this Court, Changsha ShunMou Company was dissolved due to a shareholders' resolution and deregistered. The Tangshan Ceramics Association clearly asserted that the two shareholders of the company, Li and Zhang, should bear legal liability. Li and Zhang agreed to be liable for the outstanding debts of Changsha ShunMou Company to the extent of their subscribed capital contributions. This Court holds that, although Li and Zhang signed a letter of commitment when handling the deregistration, claiming that Changsha ShunMou Company had completed the liquidation of its claims and debts, as liquidation members with statutory obligations, they failed to provide evidence such as prepared balance sheets and property lists, and the status of the company's remaining assets is unclear. Therefore, they failed to perform liquidation obligations in accordance with the law. Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (I), as amended in 2020, provides: "A company shall apply for deregistration after its dissolution has been completed in accordance with the law. If a company is deregistered without liquidation, making it impossible to liquidate the company, and a creditor claims that the shareholders of a limited liability company, the directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, and the actual controller of the company shall bear the liability for paying off the company's debts, the people's court shall support it in accordance with the law. If a company is deregistered without liquidation in accordance with the law, and a shareholder or a third party promises to bear responsibility for the company's debts when handling the deregistration with the company registration authority, and the creditor claims that the shareholder or third party shall bear corresponding civil liability for the company's debts, the people's court shall support it in accordance with the law." Therefore, Li and Zhang shall jointly and severally bear the compensation liability to the Tangshan Ceramics Association.

In summary, the retrial claims of the Tangshan Ceramics Association are partially sustained, and this Court hereby supports them. Pursuant to Article 15 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 2, 8, and 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2019); Article 122, Article 214, paragraph 1, and Article 177, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2021); Articles 2, 17, and 23 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China; and Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (I) (as amended in 2020), the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2020) Ji Min Zhong No. 104 of the Hebei High People's Court and the civil judgment (2019) Ji 02 Min Chu No. 448 of the Tangshan Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province are hereby reversed;

2. Within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, Li and Zhang shall jointly and severally compensate the Tangshan Ceramics Association for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 50,000;

3. The other claims of the Tangshan Ceramics Association are hereby dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2021).

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 2,300; court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 2,300; both shall be borne by Li and Zhang.

This judgment is final.
